subject: Planned westus4 node swap & driver refresh — coordination and canary request
messages:
From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: sam.jenkins@acme-acme.com, ops@acme-acme.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Planned westus4 node swap & driver refresh — coordination and canary request

Hi Sam / Acme ops team,

Heads up — we’ve scheduled a rolling node swap and driver refresh in westus4 to address a latency regression observed at high sequence lengths. The maintenance is planned for Sun, 14 Sep 2025 and will follow a staged canary + ramp pattern. High-level details:

- Window: 2025-09-14 01:00–05:00 UTC (we’ll run canaries starting 01:30 UTC)
- Scope: targeted driver upgrade (v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0) + two-node hardware handoff per AZ (no mass reboot)
- Expected customer impact: brief TCP connection resets for in-flight streaming requests on affected nodes (typical reconnection < 30s). No model changes.
- Rollback: automated rollback to v2.3.1 in <15 minutes if errors exceed thresholds.

Attachments: maintenance runbook + Acme-specific impact matrix attached. Please review the canary plan (attached) and confirm:
1) Is the proposed window acceptable for Acme production traffic?
2) Who is our primary on-call for coordination and verification on the day?

If you prefer a different window we can shift to a later UTC slot (we have availability Sun 14 Sep 23:00–03:00 UTC as alternative).

Next steps on our side: we’ll start with a single canary node (Route traffic to canary tag) and monitor 1) 95th P50/P95 token latency, 2) streaming disconnects, and 3) error rate for 15-minute rolling windows. We’ll share live telemetry links during the operation.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: westus4-driver-refresh-runbook-v1.2.pdf; acme-impact-matrix.csv
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme-acme.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-acme.com
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Planned westus4 node swap & driver refresh — coordination and canary request

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the detailed plan. A few quick notes from Acme ops: 

- The proposed 01:00–05:00 UTC window on 14 Sep is acceptable in general, but we have a partner launch at 02:30 UTC that day and would prefer the canary complete before that if possible. Can you run the canary at 01:00 UTC and finish the first verification cycle by 01:45 UTC?
- Please add extended telemetry for our routing tier (we need request-level connect/disconnect traces for 01:00–03:00 UTC).
- Is it possible to run the initial canary on a single AZ that does not serve our low-latency reserved instances? We want to avoid impacting reserved real-time flows.

POD/ops contact for the maintenance: Sam Jenkins (ops@acme-acme.com), reachable by mobile: +1-415-555-0134.

Also please confirm whether this operation will require us to approve an SLA credit if we see >3 minutes of sustained degradation for reserved flows.

Best,
Sam
Director, Platform Ops — Acme Data

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, sam.jenkins@acme-acme.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Planned westus4 node swap & driver refresh — coordination and canary request

Sam — thanks for the fast reply and the launch timing heads-up. A few operational clarifications and commitments: 

- Canary timing: we can begin the canary at 01:00 UTC and run the first verification cycle from 01:00–01:20 UTC. We’ll hold on further ramp until Acme confirms the 01:20 status. If the canary looks clean we’ll proceed with a second canary node at 01:40 UTC.
- AZ targeting: we can pin the canary to AZ-a in westus4 which does not host your reserved low-latency pool. That will isolate the initial traffic.
- Telemetry: we’ll enable request-level connect/disconnect traces and provide a link to a live log stream (expect a 1–2 min ingest delay).
- SLA credit: if reserved flows experience >3 minutes of sustained degradation attributable to our maintenance, we will initiate an SLA review and remediate with credits per the SLA; we’ll flag this to Finance and Customer Success proactively.

Operational notes for internal team (copying straight into the runbook):
- During the swap, ensure KV cache warmup on the canary node before diverting traffic back. If warmup fails twice we abort and rollback.
- Watch for specific driver error code 0x4E (stream rebind failure) — threshold is >0.5% errors across 15m.

Sam: please confirm that the above is acceptable and share the preferred POC mobile for the on-day bridge. If everything looks good I’ll upload an updated runbook (v1.2 -> v1.3) and trigger the DocuSign sign-off for scheduling.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Planned westus4 node swap & driver refresh — coordination and canary request

Sam — thanks, that works. Confirming final plan: 

- Canary start: 2025-09-14 01:00 UTC (AZ-a only)
- First verification window: 01:00–01:20 UTC (we’ll share telemetry links and a brief status poke at 01:25 UTC)
- Second canary node: 01:40–02:00 UTC (if first is green)
- Full ramp: proceed only after two green canaries; otherwise we rollback and reschedule.

On SLA credits: agreed — if reserved flows show >3 minutes sustained degradation we’ll open a ticket for SLA review immediately and pre-authorize a credit assessment. We’ll also notify your CSM and Finance.

On-day POC: Sam Jenkins (mobile +1-415-555-0134). Please also add Maya from your networking team if you want packet-level captures.

I’ve attached the updated runbook (v1.3) and a short canary playbook (canary-plan-20250914.md) — please review and sign the DocuSign when you’re ready. We’ll hold the operation until we receive confirmation from you (reply-all OK).

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth run.

Priyom Das
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Operations
Redwood Inference
